title: Clipboard and permission handling
learningObjectives: Explain clipboard and permission handling and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: The Clipboard API offers asynchronous read and write methods in secure contexts, subject to permission and user-activation rules. Clipboard operations can fail and should be initiated by a clear user action with useful feedback.
understand.whyItMatters: Clipboard access should be transparent and limited to the user's requested action. Provide selectable text as a fallback and never silently read clipboard contents.
understand.analogy: The clipboard is shared workspace space; the user should know when the page is placing or reading information there.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: The copy is attempted after a button click. Browser support, secure context, and permission rules still apply.

examples.explanation: The copy is attempted after a button click. Browser support, secure context, and permission rules still apply.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Add a Copy button with success/error feedback and a selectable fallback snippet.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: When should a page normally initiate a clipboard write?
questions.explanation: Clipboard writes are subject to secure-context and user-activation or permission requirements.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach when using browser APIs?
options: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.answer: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.explanation: Browser features need graceful fallback, privacy-aware permission, and lifecycle management.
